knowledge:
- key_parameters: primary_gene_id=Specifies the column containing primary gene IDs in the query GTF to assist matchGeneInfo ;; secondary_gene_id=Specifies the column containing secondary gene IDs in the query GTF to assist matchGeneInfo ;; refine.by=Determines the criteria for subsetting novel transcripts in subsetNewTranscripts (e.g., "intron" to shortlist transcripts with distinct intronic coordinates only) ;; rescale_introns=Set to TRUE in viewTranscripts to shrink introns and display exonic regions and CDSs more clearly ;; plot=Set to TRUE in predictDomains to plot domain architectures for the query proteins ;; progress_bar=Set to FALSE in predictDomains to suppress the progress bar
- alternatives: AnnotationHub can be used to retrieve reference transcriptomes (GTF/GFF3) and genome sequences (2bit files) as an alternative to direct FTP downloads from GENCODE or Ensembl. BSgenome packages can be used to load genome sequences instead of importing FASTA files.
- when_to_use: Use when you have a custom-assembled transcriptome (from bulk, single-cell, or long-read RNA-seq data) in GTF format and want to perform functional annotation, including matching to official gene IDs, identifying novel isoforms, predicting coding sequences (CDS), and predicting NMD susceptibility and protein domains.
- pitfalls: Ensure that the custom GTF file contains both gene_id and transcript_id attributes. Chromosome naming styles (e.g., "chr1" vs "1") must match between the custom transcriptome, reference transcriptome, and genome sequence; use matchChromosomes() to resolve mismatches. predictDomains() requires a stable internet connection to query the online PFAM database and can be slow; it is recommended to test on a small subset of genes first.

workflows.name: custom_transcriptome_annotation
workflows.intent: Perform functional annotation of a custom-assembled transcriptome by matching gene metadata, filtering for novel transcripts, predicting coding sequences, and analyzing NMD susceptibility and protein domains.
input: custom_assembled_transcriptome.gtf (custom-assembled transcriptome in GTF format containing gene_id and transcript_id attributes)
reference_transcriptome.gtf (reference transcriptome annotation in GTF/GFF3 format)
genome_sequence (BSgenome object, 2bit file, or FASTA file containing genomic DNA sequence)
workflows.stages: 1. Import custom GTF using importGTF ;; 2. Match gene metadata to reference using matchGeneInfo ;; 3. Subset novel transcripts using subsetNewTranscripts ;; 4. Build CDS information using buildCDS and a genome sequence ;; 5. Predict NMD susceptibility using predictNMD ;; 6. Predict protein domains using predictDomains ;; 7. Export annotated GTF and prediction tables using rtracklayer::export and write.table
workflows.code:
library (factR)
gtf <- system.file ( "extdata" , "sc_merged_sample.gtf.gz" , package = "factR" )
custom.gtf <- importGTF (gtf)
tmp <- tempfile ()
download.file ( "ftp://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_mouse/release_M25/gencode.vM25.annotation.gtf.gz" , destfile = tmp)
ref.gtf <- importGTF (tmp)
custom_matched_2.gtf <- matchGeneInfo (custom.gtf, ref.gtf, primary_gene_id = "gene_id" , secondary_gene_id = "ref_gene_id" )
custom_new.gtf <- subsetNewTranscripts (custom_matched_2.gtf, ref.gtf, refine.by = "intron" )
library (BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10)
Mmusculus <- BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10
custom_new_CDS.gtf <- buildCDS (custom_new.gtf, ref.gtf, Mmusculus)
NMDprediction.out <- predictNMD (custom_new_CDS.gtf)
domains.out <- predictDomains (custom_new_CDS.gtf, Mmusculus, progress_bar = FALSE )
library (rtracklayer)
export (custom_new_CDS.gtf, "Custom_new.gtf" , format = "GTF" )
write.table (NMDprediction.out, "Custom_new_NMD.txt" , sep = " \t " , row.names = FALSE , quote = FALSE )
write.table (domains.out, "Custom_new_domains.txt" , sep = " \t " , row.names = FALSE , quote = FALSE )
